info.title: HYDRA-UMC-SERVER API
info.description: Real, hand-verified OpenAPI description of HYDRA-UMC-SERVER's own public HTTP surface (src/server.ts) - the SDK's own charter (docs/API_DESIGN.md) commits to publishing 'the OpenAPI source and typed clients', and this is its first real slice, not a placeholder. Deliberately covers only the routes an external/typed client actually needs to discover a server, read/write its fleet roster, and dispatch a real-time robot command - the read/command/real-time planes docs/API_DESIGN.md itself separates. It is NOT a full inventory of every route in server.ts: admin-only account/log/integration management, camera process supervision, CAN-OTA firmware transfer, and power/system-service control are real, but operational rather than SDK-contract surface, and are intentionally left for a later slice (see the 'still out of scope' note at the end of this description). One real, disclosed discrepancy: docs/API_DESIGN.md describes command results using ACCEPTED/REJECTED/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED plus a correlation identifier - POST /api/robot/{id}/command's own real implementation does not (yet) return that envelope; it replies with a plain {success, affectedCount} once the mutation has already been applied and broadcast. This document describes the real, current behavior, not the aspirational one - fixing that gap is Server-side product work, out of scope for this SDK.

servers.description: HYDRA-UMC-SERVER's own default bind address (see HYDRA-UMC-SERVER/src/server.ts's defaultServerURL-equivalent and HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own defaultServerURL, which both point here).

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: Unauthenticated server identity/health, per docs/CONTRACTS.md's ServerDiscovery contract.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: JWT issuance for every other authenticated route below.

tags.name: fleet
tags.description: The real controller/robot roster - the read plane docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

tags.name: command
tags.description: Real-time, per-robot atomic commands - the command plane docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

get.summary: Real server identity and discovery metadata
get.description: Unauthenticated by default. Real, per-client remote-access gating (Config > Remote Access) can make this respond 404 for a given X-Hydra-Client caller instead of exposing whether a server exists at all at that address.

parameters.name: X-Hydra-Client
parameters.description: Identifies which real client is asking (e.g. suite, android, ios), so the per-client remote-access gate in Config can allow/deny it independently of the others.

200.description: Real server identity, mirroring the published ServerDiscovery contract (contracts/json-schema/v1/server-discovery.schema.json).

404.description: Remote access is disabled for this X-Hydra-Client caller - deliberately indistinguishable from 'no server running here' to a scanning client. Empty body.

post.summary: Authenticate with a local username/password and obtain a JWT

200.description: Real JWT issued - pass it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every route below tagged with bearerAuth.

401.description: Real invalid-credentials rejection - same message for an unknown username and a wrong password, on purpose (never confirms which one was wrong).

get.summary: Read the real, current full settings document, including the controller/robot roster
get.description: Unauthenticated real read - the same contract HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own `robots`/`doctor` commands already consume. The `settings` object is intentionally NOT modeled field-by-field here: the server itself treats it as an opaque, forward-compatible blob (see docs/CONTRACTS.md's own 'producers can add compatible fields without breaking older consumers') - only the `controllers` roster actually consumed by real typed clients today is modeled below.

500.description: The settings file on disk could not be read.

post.summary: Replace the real settings document (admin only)
post.description: Real, admin-only write. Persists the payload verbatim (queued, debounced disk write) and broadcasts it to every other connected client - and, on a real HYDRA-UMC-SERVER build with the camera process supervisor, reconciles each camera's own capture process against its new configuration.

post.summary: Dispatch one real, atomic, broadcast command to a robot (and its combined sibling, where the command type fans out)
post.description: Real command plane: mutates in-memory state, queues a debounced full-settings write, and broadcasts a small per-robot delta to every other connected client via the same request/response cycle - there is no separate polling step. See this document's own top-level description for the real (not the aspirational ACCEPTED/REJECTED/... ) response shape.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A real robot's own numeric id (distinct from a controller's own, sometimes string, id - see HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own robots.go for that real, confirmed API inconsistency).

200.description: Real, applied mutation - see this document's own top-level description for why this is not the ACCEPTED/REJECTED/... envelope docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

400.description: No settings loaded yet, or (for `trajectory`) a real, rejected point list - too few/many points, a non-finite field, an unsupported motionType, or table axes on a robot with no configured XY table.

404.description: No robot with this id exists in the current settings document.

ServerDiscovery.description: Mirrors contracts/json-schema/v1/server-discovery.schema.json field-for-field - restated here natively rather than $ref'd across schema drafts, since that file's own $id/$schema target JSON Schema 2020-12 directly rather than through OpenAPI's Schema Object.

token.description: A signed JWT (see JWT_EXPIRES_IN for this server's own configured lifetime, default 30d).

role.description: e.g. "admin" or "operator" - see docs/CONTRACTS.md's account-management notes.

RobotRosterEntry.description: Only the roster-level fields real typed clients (e.g. HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own robots.go) actually consume are modeled - a real robot object carries many more live-state fields (pos, joints, playbackState, valves, pumps, camera, xyTable, ...) not exhaustively typed here, matching this contract's own additive philosophy.

id.description: A real robot's own numeric id - distinct from a controller's own id, which may be a string.

combinedWith.description: Sibling robot ids that share this robot's non-trajectory commands (see the command plane's own affectedIds rule).

id.description: A real controller's own id - may be a string (e.g. "localhost" for the default local controller) even though a robot's own id is always numeric; a real, confirmed API inconsistency, not a typo.

SettingsDocument.description: The real, full settings document persisted to data/settings.json. `settings` is deliberately left opaque (type: object only) - it carries UI layout, integrations, gamepad mapping, and other fields the server itself treats as an untyped blob it never validates; only `controllers` is modeled to roster depth, since that is the real, stable surface existing typed clients already depend on.

affectedCount.description: How many robots this one command actually touched - more than 1 only for a non-trajectory command on a combined pair (see combinedWith).

CommandStop.description: Stops playback now (also stops this robot's own server-side playback timer) and clears isPlaying/activeStep/isPaused/isFinished.

CommandPlay.description: Starts playback from step 0 (also starts this robot's own server-side playback timer).

CommandPause.description: Toggles pause by default; `params.paused` sets an explicit desired state instead, so a combined pair can never end up with one paused member and one not.

CommandJog.description: Relative (or, with absolute:true, absolute) single-axis motion. target:"xytable" only honors axis x/y and requires the robot to have a configured XY table; target:"robot" (default) applies to any of x/y/z/a/b/c and accepts an optional client-computed joints override (validated as 6 finite numbers, else the server falls back to its own generic IK).

absolute.description: Set the axis to amount instead of adding amount to it.

joints.description: Optional client-computed joint override, only honored for target:"robot".

CommandReset.description: target:"robot" (default) zeroes pos/joints to home (tx/ty/trz preserved); target:"xytable" zeroes only the XY table's own pos and pos.tx/ty, leaving the arm's own pose untouched.

joints.description: Optional client-supplied home pose (e.g. a per-model homePoseFor(robot.model)); falls back to the server's own generic IK if omitted/invalid.

CommandJogStep.description: Sets this robot's own server-synced jog step size, used by subsequent "jog" commands' own client-side amount calculation.

CommandReset3D.description: Signals every OTHER connected client to remount its own local 3D camera view for this robot - no real robot motion or state change.

CommandTool.description: Sets the robot's currently mounted end-effector/tool label.

CommandValve.description: Sets one pneumatic valve's open/closed state.

CommandPump.description: Sets one vacuum pump's on/off state.

CommandSpeed.description: Sets playback speed and/or acceleration, each independently optional; at least one is expected to be present for this command to have any effect.

CommandTrajectory.description: Loads and selects a full point list as this robot's own Work, validated and prepared BEFORE any state is touched (so a racing Play command can never replay a stale trajectory). Unlike every other command, this never applies to a combined sibling - a trajectory belongs to exactly one robot.

TrajectoryPoint.description: Every field is optional per point, but the point must carry either all 6 native joints (j1..j6) or a full Cartesian pose (x, y, z) - checked after this shape validates. tx/ty/trz (XY table axes) are only accepted on a robot with a configured XY table.

CommandVision.description: Enables/disables this robot's own vision pipeline, and its assigned camera's connected flag alongside it.
